report.source_text: To further characterize the condition, a chest/abdomen CT scan was performed. The CT images revealed a large heterogeneous enhancing mass measuring 22.5×16.5×22.5 cm in the right lower hemithorax. The mass did not involve the rib cage but exerted pressure on the adjacent lung and cardiomediastinal structures, including the superior vena cava, right atrium, and right pulmonary vein. A large pleural fibroma was hypothesized based on these findings (Fig. 2). CT scan did not show any adenopathy, other mass lesions, or bone metastasis.

report.source_text: A biochemical work-up for hypoglycaemia revealed non-insulin-mediated hypoglycemia with a blood glucose level of 25 mg/dL (normal range: 70-99 mg/dL). Furthermore, there were concomitant low serum insulin levels (1 microIU/mL, normal range: 6-27 microIU/mL), low serum C-peptide levels (<0.5 microg/L, normal range: 0.5-4.0 microg/L), and low serum IGF-1 levels for sex and age (60 mcg/L, below the 1st percentile). The pituitary function was found to be normal, and cortisol deficiency was ruled out. Additionally, insulin antibodies tested negative. The renal and hepatic functions were within normal limits. A complete blood count and metabolic panel excluded anemia and electrolyte imbalances (Table 2).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 59-year-old male presented with recurrent fasting hypoglycemia, excessive sweating, tremors, weakness, and dyspnea. Initial workup revealed a large heterogeneous enhancing mass (22.5x16.5x22.5 cm) in the right lower hemithorax on chest CT, compressing cardiac structures. Biochemical analysis during hypoglycemia showed low blood glucose (25 mg/dL) with concomitantly low serum insulin (1 microIU/mL), low C-peptide (<0.5 microg/L), and low IGF-1 (60 mcg/L), consistent with non-insulin-mediated hypoglycemia (NICTH). Histopathological examination of the mass confirmed a Solitary Fibrous Tumor of the Pleura (SFTP) with characteristic spindle-shaped cells and positive immunohistochemical staining for Bcl-2, STAT6, and CD34. The patient underwent surgical resection of the mass, leading to immediate normalization of serum glucose levels and complete resolution of dyspnea and hypoglycemic episodes post-operatively.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with recurrent fasting hypoglycemia, excessive sweating, tremors, weakness, and dyspnea.

Chest CT revealed a large heterogeneous enhancing mass (22.5x16.5x22.5 cm) in the right lower hemithorax, hypothesized as a pleural fibroma, and echocardiography showed compression of the right atrial cavity.

Biochemical workup during hypoglycemia showed non-insulin-mediated hypoglycemia with blood glucose 25 mg/dL, low serum insulin (1 microIU/mL), low serum C-peptide (<0.5 microg/L), and low serum IGF-1 (60 mcg/L), supporting NICTH.

Histopathological evaluation of the resected mass showed spindle-shaped cells with no nuclear pleomorphism or necrosis, and immunohistochemical analysis was positive for Bcl-2, STAT6, and CD34, confirming Solitary Fibrous Tumor of the Pleura (SFTP).
The patient underwent right posterolateral open thoracotomy for mass resection.
Post-operative serum glucose levels normalized, and hypoglycemic episodes and dyspnea completely resolved, confirming the causal link between the tumor and hypoglycemia.
